reason: B proposes the more physically credible governing mechanism for sliding in air at 600–800°C: selective oxidation and a continuous tribo-oxide can reduce metal contact, adhesive wear, and subsurface plastic flow, whereas Cu-rich precipitates are likely soft and prone to coarsening rather than reliably strengthening this alloy at high temperature. B is also testable through paired wear tests and oxide/segregation characterization, although its assumed anneal-induced Cr/Fe grain-boundary segregation lacks cited support and should be independently verified.
